text:
maya: Heads-up — prod is seeing a small class of streaming requests that end up hanging after ~30s with no data despite the backend still writing chunks. Repro on canary in eu-west but not in every region. :thinking:

aj: Any logs? proxy or client side?

maya: Proxy logs show we suppressed heartbeats because bytes were seen recently, but the browser client read loop blocks until a full event boundary arrives. Chunks are often 'partial' events. Example payload frag: 
```
data: {"id":"x", "chunk": true}

---then later---
data: {"id":"x", "chunk": false}

```
So our "activity" check treats any bytes as activity and skips sending keepalive pings. That hides the fact the client hasn't received a complete event.

lucas: Oof. The suppression rule was to avoid pinging when backends stream frequently. But with chunked event framing this causes silent stalls for slow readers.

aj: How does this show up in telemetry today?

maya: Console shows a spike in "stream stalls" (users reporting stuck streams) while per-route heartbeat_sent = 0. We don't currently emit a metric for suppressed heartbeats or for last_client_read_time.

infra-bot: ALERT: sse_stream_stall_count increased by 320% in us-west-2 in the last hour.

sam: Workaround for some customers was toggling edge buffering/flush thresholds, but that's brittle.

lucas: Proposal: change suppression logic to consider event boundaries. Only suppress heartbeat if the last seen bytes end with an event separator ("\n\n") or contain a full `event:`/`data:` pair. Otherwise treat as "partial activity" and still send a heartbeat after a short timeout (eg 5s).

aj: Two config knobs we need to debate: default heartbeat timeout (5s vs 15s) and whether to expose an override header (e.g., `X-Stream-Idle-Threshold`) customers can set per-route.

sam: I'm for exposing a header; default should err on fewer pings for high QPS routes (15s). But for interactive UIs we can document lowering it.

maya: UX/console side: add metrics `heartbeat_suppressed_count` and `partial_chunk_bytes` to per-route dashboard. We should also surface last_full_event_age and last_client_ack_time in the route inspector.

lucas: Rollout plan: implement parser-aware suppression in proxy, ship metric, enable in 10% canary, observe `sse_stream_stall_count` and `heartbeat_suppressed_count` for 24h, ramp to 50/100 if no regressions. Add auto-rollback if stall_count > 2x baseline in 15m window.

aj: Tests: unit test for chunked parser that feeds partial chunks and asserts heartbeat is emitted after timeout. E2E: slow-client test in infra harness.

maya: I'll draft the PR. Runbook notes for oncall: 
- If stall spike, set route header `X-Stream-Idle-Threshold: 15` as a temporary mitigation.
- If user impact persists, rollback proxy canary.

aj: Thanks. @lucas can you add the dashboard panels and an alert query? :thumbsup:

lucas: On it. Using a log query: 
```
filter: sse.stream and heartbeat_suppressed=true | stats count() by route, region
```
Added panels under Observability -> Streaming -> "Heartbeat suppression" and a link in the incident runbook.

sam: I'll make sure release notes mention the new header and the default change.

lucas: (later) Panels live: https://console/redwood/d/streaming-heartbeat  - watchers added to eng-runtime.

maya: Great, tracking in the PR description and will include recommended console queries.

End of thread.
